about: Which error code and HTTP status each backend answers with, on the wire. Shared byte-for-byte with the PHP twin (particle-academy/fancy-passkeys, tests/fixtures/errors/codes.json); change both in the same session. `codes` is the closed set: every code's status and the code a client is shown (`wire`; three codes that would reveal something about a stored credential are redacted to verification_failed). `ceremonies` pins what a named failure answers, so the two backends cannot drift apart on it again: until 2026-11-13 a wrong-origin assertion was origin_not_allowed 400 from Node and verification_failed 401 from PHP. A wrong origin is decided BEFORE the credential is looked up, so the answer is the same whether or not the credential exists and the code is not an existence oracle.

ceremonies.name: wrong-origin-assertion
ceremonies.why: An assertion whose clientDataJSON origin is not on the allow-list, for a credential the server holds.

ceremonies.name: wrong-origin-assertion-unknown-credential
ceremonies.why: The same assertion for a credential the server has never seen. It must answer exactly as above, or the origin check is a credential-existence oracle.

ceremonies.name: wrong-origin-registration
ceremonies.why: A registration response whose clientDataJSON origin is not on the allow-list.
